confirmed_source_facts.fact: For nonnegative int-tagged keys on arrays, indexed descriptor lookup runs before the dense element load.
Descriptor lookup formats the usize index as a String, looks up its atom, then probes the descriptor map.
Array writes can call array_descriptor repeatedly before the element write or generic fallback.
Descriptor insertion/removal and array-length truncation are split across multiple owner paths; a per-array summary flag would need derived updates at all these transitions.

corrections: Value::number canonicalizes integral f64 values in the i32 range to int-tagged Values, except negative zero. The supplied small-index timing does not establish that those keys take a double slow path.
The heap collection threshold is already survivor-scaled after collection and has a 384-allocation floor; the generic proposal to make it survivor-proportional is already present.

qualification.reported_microbenchmarks: User-supplied batch 7 timings were not independently rerun and include no stored scripts, raw samples, binary hash, or profile artifact.
qualification.implementation: No code change. Treat the unconditional descriptor lookup as a profile lead, not a demonstrated benchmark win.
next_evidence: Store the exact guest scripts, Quench and Node --jitless commands, paired raw timings, source/build hashes, and a symbolized profile for array read/write cases.

Before adding a per-array flag, audit descriptor insertion/removal, freeze/seal, defineProperty, array-length shrink, inherited index accessors, arguments objects, proxies, and typed-array boundaries.
After Stage A, measure the common descriptor-free array path and verify exact fallback behavior against affected Test262 stages and the local Node oracle.
